name: Finished part photo check
summary: Logs each finished-part check request from the inbox into the business's own check register, then drafts the result email once a person has recorded a pass, fail or second look. Crons read and draft; a person approves every email before it sends.

covered_by.photograph-part: not covered (the person takes the photos)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: New finished-part check requests from the inbox folder.

crons.name: register
crons.summary: One row per new request in the check register, status Awaiting photo check.

crons.name: report
crons.summary: Draft the result email for each recorded result and queue its send for approval.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads of the request folder, a new row in the check register, and an Outlook draft that stays unsent. The only operation that reaches a customer is the send of that draft, and it is queued for approval.

microsoft-365.covers: request folder read, check register rows, result email drafts and their approved send

gaps: MRPeasy: no kit folder under core/sdk/platforms, so nothing can be called. Its quality control pages cover receiving, inspection and rework, but no operation is mapped.
Odoo: the kit folder exists but its ops file is empty, so no operation is callable. Every Odoo step rests on community forum answers.
Sitemate: no kit folder, so nothing can be called. Its photo tags and defect reports are the closest match to this job once mapped.
Google Workspace is mapped in the kit (Drive and Sheets) but has no adapter here. Add one if a client keeps its photos or register there.
Only Microsoft 365 is built, and its adapter is docs-only until a sandbox tenant proves it.
Confirm the workflow steps and platform coverage with the business before enabling its crons.
Photographing, measuring and comparing a part to a drawing are judgment steps for the person or the agent. No platform in the kit performs them.
No command yet records the result (pass, fail or second look) that the report cron reads. Until one exists, the result is written to the check's store record by hand.
Rework, scrap, release and dispatch are not covered. Those stay in the business's own system.
The inbox search term defaults to 'photo', which is a guess. Confirm it with the client.
